A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAPG research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Countdown and mathematical-benchmark experiments, training curves, offloading-ratio analyses and response case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds reward/group-size ablations, router diagnostics, cloud-call measurements and early-exit examples.

M1.justification: The constrained objective, hierarchical reward, prompt templates, group-gradient estimator and adaptive filtering remain the same. The estimator's rewritten coefficient is algebraically equivalent. Pseudocode clarification, caching disclosure and examples of emergent early exit do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Countdown, MATH-lighteval, MATH-500, AMC23, AIME24 and MinervaMath. The new ablations and case studies remain within the existing mathematical-reasoning coverage.

E2.justification: The baseline membership is unchanged, and Dr. GRPO is discussed without reported empirical comparison. However, v2 explicitly specifies query-plus-local-response inputs for Task-Tuning&Router, whereas v1 provides a prompt-based formulation without that experimental detail. The PDFs do not resolve whether this revises the comparator or clarifies its implementation.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix B adds reward-weight sweeps evaluated without the cloud-call budget and training with group sizes 4, 8, 16 and 32. These introduce controlled experimental settings while retaining the original dataset splits, numerical default hyperparameters and main evaluation budget.

E4.justification: v2 adds reward-weight and group-size ablations, router convergence/generalization diagnostics, training cloud-call cost analysis and an early-exit case study in Appendices B and F–H. These substantially expand investigation of component behavior and efficiency. The original offloading-ratio analysis and Countdown examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental run/seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 6's new averaging is across two model-specific routers; the new estimator-variance proof concerns theoretical properties rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Tables 2–3 report reward/group-size sensitivity results, Table 6 reports training cloud-call counts, and Figures 6–7 add router-learning results. Table 1 revises router average accuracy from 49.8 to 51.6 for Qwen2.5-1.5B and 44.3 to 48.5 for Llama-3.2-3B. The proposed method's corresponding averages remain 56.2 and 55.5.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 expands beyond unbiasedness to an O(1/G) covariance/variance property. New Lemma D.1 and Appendices D.2–D.3 derive the covariance expression and scaling result. Appendix A.2 also introduces a Dr. GRPO objective and mathematical argument absent from v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion soften the stated role of adaptive filtering from enforcing or constraining cloud usage to providing complementary learning signals. The central claims of joint problem-solving/routing through RL, stable training and superior benchmark performance remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about reward-controlled offloading, sufficient group diversity, router generalization, training cloud-call costs and naturally emerging early exit. It also critiques Dr. GRPO's suitability. A new limitations paragraph identifies dependence on verifiable mathematical rewards and the need for reliable quality rewards for open-ended tasks.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents caching cloud responses across training iterations, router inputs and truncating calls when evaluating Collaboration-Aware Tuning at lower budgets. It corrects the swapped model-size labels in the hyperparameter-table header. Existing prompts, data-split instructions and hardware specifications are retained.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 expands positioning around RL reasoning, search, tool use and agents, adding works including Search-R1, ReTool, DAPO and Minions. Remark 3.3 and Appendix A.2 introduce a substantive comparison with Dr. GRPO. The earlier ReMax/RLOO discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are substantially revised toward collaborative reasoning. The GRPO-failure discussion moves from the main method section into Appendix A, experiments gain a nested Main Results structure, and the appendices are extensively reorganized around the new analyses.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with resized and relocated figures and tables. The GRPO-failure plot moves to the appendix, three experimental tables and two router plots are added, and the retained response examples are substantially compressed and reformatted.

improvement.justification: The new variance proof and targeted ablations strengthen support for GAPG's stability and configuration choices, while router diagnostics, caching disclosure and explicit applicability limits improve transparency. These gains are tempered by Appendix A.2 dropping likelihood ratios when rewriting Dr. GRPO's objective, weakening its length-based critique, and by the retained '6–8 points' claim despite the revised 4.6-point Qwen average gap in Table 1.
